caveats: unique_destination_ips uses TargetObject as a proxy for IP addresses (same proxy as training SILRAD benign windows — not a new approximation).
SILRAD attack labels are binary (class=1) without named ransomware family attribution.
Temporal chunking (10 events/window) without process-level grouping may produce ~10-20% mixed-process windows whose majority label is attack even if some events are benign in context.
event_26_count (FileDeleteDetected) is absent from SILRAD attack events in the raw data; filled with 0 as per standard missing-feature handling.

data_provenance.leakage_note: Attack windows (class=1): CONFIRMED not present in any training/validation/test split — prepare_live_data.py explicitly filters class==0 only. Benign companion windows: OVERLAP with training data (same SILRAD benign pool). The benign companion is included only for balanced metric calculation. Attack-class metrics (TP/FN/recall) are leakage-free.
data_provenance.window_label_noise_warning: Sequential chunking without process-level grouping may produce ~10-20% windows whose majority-vote label is '1' despite containing some benign events. This causes conservative (understated) recall estimates.

leakage_assessment.verdict: NO OVERLAP: SILRAD attack windows (class=1) were never loaded into any training, validation, or test split. The source tags 'SILRAD_RANSOMWARE_ATTACK' / 'silrad_dataset_log_*' were only assigned to class=0 benign windows. The SILRAD attack events are a genuinely unseen evaluation set for the two-stage pipeline.
leakage_assessment.benign_companion_leakage: Benign companion windows overlap with training data (same SILRAD CSV, class=0). This affects TN/FP/FPR calculations. Attack-class metrics (TP, FN, recall, precision) are unaffected by benign companion overlap.
leakage_assessment.exact_byte_level_overlap: Exact byte-level deduplication was not performed. The SILRAD adapter applies sequential chunking — chunk boundaries differ between attack-only and full-file runs. This is a known limitation: we cannot rule out feature-level statistical similarity between attack windows and any benign SILRAD windows, but source-level exclusion confirms no attack record was ever loaded during training.

limitations: Sequential chunking without process-level grouping may produce mixed-process attack windows (~10-20% label noise), causing conservative (understated) recall.
SILRAD attack labels are binary (0/1); no named ransomware family attribution is available.
Benign companion windows are sampled from the same SILRAD benign pool used in training; TN/FP/FPR calculations should be treated as indicative only.
unique_destination_ips uses TargetObject as a proxy for network destinations — same approximation used during SILRAD benign training data.
Exact byte-level deduplication not performed; source-level exclusion confirmed only.
academic_safe_interpretation: On the SILRAD cross-source evaluation subset (SILRAD attack events, class=1, never seen during training), the existing trained two-stage pipeline (Isolation Forest + BiLSTM) achieved the metrics stated in results.classification_metrics. These results represent external validation on a genuinely unseen attack source using the same 17-feature Sysmon representation. The SILRAD dataset originates from a distinct collection environment and contributes attack telemetry not present in any training or standard held-out evaluation split.
